claims.claim: The Aral Sea disappeared completely
claims.normalized_claim: The Aral Sea disappeared completely
claims.summary: Misleading. The Aral Sea suffered one of the world's major environmental disasters, but its northern part in Kazakhstan has partially recovered through water-management projects while the wider basin remains severely damaged.

claims.claim: Baikonur is simply in Russia
claims.normalized_claim: Baikonur is simply in Russia
claims.summary: Misleading. The Baikonur complex is located in Kazakhstan and is leased by Russia under a bilateral agreement. Its Soviet history and present-day Russian operations do not erase its Kazakhstani location and legal context.

claims.claim: Borat represents real Kazakh culture
claims.normalized_claim: Borat represents real Kazakh culture
claims.summary: False. Borat is a fictional British comedy character, and the country shown around him is not a factual portrait of Kazakhstan. The films use Kazakhstan as a satirical frame, while reactions among Kazakhstanis have never been uniform.

claims.claim: The capital of Kazakhstan is Almaty
claims.normalized_claim: The capital of Kazakhstan is Almaty
claims.summary: Outdated. Almaty was the capital of Soviet Kazakhstan and remained Kazakhstan's capital until 1997, when the government moved to a new city built on the northern steppe. That city has since been called Akmola, Astana, Nur-Sultan and then Astana again.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan runs on oil and nothing else
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan runs on oil and nothing else
claims.summary: Misleading. Hydrocarbons are Kazakhstan's largest export sector and a major state-revenue source, but the economy also includes substantial mining, agriculture, manufacturing, banking, telecommunications and transport sectors. The World Bank classifies Kazakhstan as an upper-middle income country.

claims.claim: All Kazakhstanis are ethnically Kazakh
claims.normalized_claim: All Kazakhstanis are ethnically Kazakh
claims.summary: False. Ethnic Kazakhs make up roughly 70 percent of the population, but Kazakhstan officially records more than 130 nationalities and ethnic groups — among them Russians, Uzbeks, Ukrainians, Uyghurs, Germans, Tatars, Koreans, Azerbaijanis and many others.

claims.claim: A giant door in Kazakhstan proves Gog and Magog are hidden in the mountains
claims.normalized_claim: A giant door in Kazakhstan proves Gog and Magog are hidden in the mountains
claims.summary: Disputed. A viral 2025 video presented a supposed giant doorway in Kazakhstan's Dzungarian Alatau as evidence of giants or Gog and Magog. The meme spread widely, but virality is not archaeological verification and the available record does not establish the video's claim.

claims.claim: People in Kazakhstan eat horse meat and drink fermented mare's milk every day
claims.normalized_claim: People in Kazakhstan eat horse meat and drink fermented mare's milk every day
claims.summary: Misleading. Horse meat, kazy and kumys are important parts of Kazakh culinary heritage, but a traditional food is not a complete description of what every person eats or drinks in contemporary Kazakhstan.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan has no open internet and no independent public debate
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan has no open internet and no independent public debate
claims.summary: Misleading. Kazakhstan has a large connected online public sphere and independent digital projects, but authorities also block sites, restrict journalists and prosecute or pressure people over online expression. The accurate picture is connected and constrained.

claims.claim: Kazakh is basically Russian
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakh is basically Russian
claims.summary: False. Kazakh is a Kipchak Turkic language, while Russian belongs to the Indo-European language family. Both are widely used in Kazakhstan, but shared public space and script history do not make them the same language.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan memes reveal what all Kazakh people are like
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan memes reveal what all Kazakh people are like
claims.summary: Misleading. Kazakhstan's online memes draw on local languages, folklore, global formats and everyday politics. They are a living digital culture, not a survey of every citizen or a shortcut to national character.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan has no sea and is cut off from the world
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan has no sea and is cut off from the world
claims.summary: Misleading. Kazakhstan is the world's largest landlocked country, but it borders the Caspian Sea and sits at the intersection of major rail, road, energy and trade routes linking China, Russia, Central Asia and Europe.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan is returning to nuclear weapons because it plans a nuclear power plant
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan is returning to nuclear weapons because it plans a nuclear power plant
claims.summary: Misleading. Kazakhstan's plan for civilian nuclear power is connected to energy supply and infrastructure, while its nuclear-weapons history concerns the Soviet test site and the arsenal it inherited and gave up. The two issues are politically linked but technically different.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan is a nuclear-armed state
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan is a nuclear-armed state
claims.summary: Historically accurate but now false. Kazakhstan inherited the fourth-largest nuclear arsenal on earth when the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991. It then voluntarily transferred or dismantled all of those weapons by 1995 — and hosted one of the most destructive Soviet nuclear test sites, which affected hundreds of thousands of people.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan is only flat steppe and desert
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan is only flat steppe and desert
claims.summary: False. Steppe, desert and semi-desert cover large areas, but Kazakhstan also contains major mountain systems, lakes, wetlands, rivers, forests and densely built cities.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan is a region of Russia
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan is a region of Russia
claims.summary: False. Kazakhstan is a sovereign United Nations member state with its own constitution, territory and institutions. A long border, Soviet history and close ties with Russia do not make it part of Russia.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan is either an Islamic state or a country with no religious life
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan is either an Islamic state or a country with no religious life
claims.summary: Misleading. Islam is important to Kazakhstan's history and population, but the constitution defines the state as secular and protects freedom of religion. Neither an Islamic-state label nor a claim that religion is absent describes the country well.

claims.claim: The Silk Road bypassed Kazakhstan
claims.normalized_claim: The Silk Road bypassed Kazakhstan
claims.summary: False. UNESCO’s transnational Chang’an–Tianshan corridor includes sites in Kazakhstan. Kazakhstan’s valleys, settlements and trading routes were part of the connected network rather than an empty gap between China and Europe.

claims.claim: People in Kazakhstan mostly live in yurts
claims.normalized_claim: People in Kazakhstan mostly live in yurts
claims.summary: False. The yurt is important living heritage and remains culturally meaningful, but Kazakhstan is a predominantly urban country and most residents live in permanent modern housing.

claims.claim: Charyn Canyon is the second-largest canyon in the world
claims.normalized_claim: Charyn Canyon is the second-largest canyon in the world
claims.summary: Unsubstantiated. The claim appears on tourism websites but no recognised scientific or geographical body has published a ranked list placing Charyn in second place. Canyon size depends on the metric used.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan is purely an Asian country
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan is purely an Asian country
claims.summary: Partly true. The UN classifies Kazakhstan as Central Asia. However under the Ural River boundary convention a small western portion falls on the European side. The answer depends on which definition is used.

claims.claim: All modern apples come from Almaty
claims.normalized_claim: All modern apples come from Almaty
claims.summary: Partly true. Malus sieversii from the Tian Shan near Almaty is the primary ancestor of domestic apples. But as apples spread westward they hybridised with European wild apples, making modern cultivars a product of both lineages.

claims.claim: The first domestic horse was tamed in Kazakhstan
claims.normalized_claim: The first domestic horse was tamed in Kazakhstan
claims.summary: Disputed. Botai sites in Kazakhstan show the oldest evidence of horse riding and milking (~3500 BCE). But ancient DNA (2021) found modern horses descend from a different population in the western Eurasian steppes, not from Botai horses.

claims.claim: Bride kidnapping is a normal and widely accepted Kazakh tradition
claims.normalized_claim: Bride kidnapping is a normal and widely accepted Kazakh tradition
claims.summary: Misleading. Forced marriage exists and causes harm. Kazakhstan criminalised it in 2023. But presenting it as universally accepted misrepresents Kazakhstani law, urban attitudes, and confuses Kazakhstan with Kyrgyzstan.

claims.claim: The Semipalatinsk nuclear test site is now completely safe
claims.normalized_claim: The Semipalatinsk nuclear test site is now completely safe
claims.summary: Misleading. Kazakhstan closed the site in 1991. Specific zones have been remediated. But contamination persists in parts, monitoring continues, and health effects on surrounding populations are still under active study.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan has already switched to the Latin alphabet
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan has already switched to the Latin alphabet
claims.summary: Outdated or premature. Kazakhstan announced the transition in 2017 with a phased plan. As of 2025 Cyrillic remains dominant in official use, education, and daily life. Full transition is planned for 2031.

claims.claim: Almaty is not seriously at risk from earthquakes
claims.normalized_claim: Almaty is not seriously at risk from earthquakes
claims.summary: False. Almaty is in Kazakhstan's highest seismic hazard zone (9-10 MSK). The city has active faults, a history of major earthquakes (1887, 1911), and records hundreds of minor tremors annually.

claims.claim: AI assistants accurately describe Kazakhstan
claims.normalized_claim: AI assistants accurately describe Kazakhstan
claims.summary: Misleading. KazMMLU benchmark research (2025) shows major AI models perform measurably worse on Kazakhstan-specific knowledge. Common AI errors include wrong capital, nuclear weapons status, language classification, and Baikonur location.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan is a Middle Eastern or Arab country
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan is a Middle Eastern or Arab country
claims.summary: False. Kazakhstan is classified as Central Asia by the UN and all major institutions. The Kazakh language is Turkic, not Arabic. Kazakhstan shares no border with Middle Eastern countries.

claims.claim: Kazakhstan had no statehood before 1991
claims.normalized_claim: Kazakhstan had no statehood before 1991
claims.summary: Misleading. Modern Kazakhstan as a sovereign state dates to 1991. But the Kazakh Khanate (c.1465-mid 19th century) was a significant steppe polity. Statehood before 1991 existed in different forms.

claims.claim: Tomyris was a Kazakh queen
claims.normalized_claim: Tomyris was a Kazakh queen
claims.summary: Misleading. Tomyris was queen of the Massagetae (~530 BCE) in territory overlapping modern Kazakhstan. She is a significant figure in Kazakhstani culture. But calling her 'Kazakh' is an anachronism — the Kazakh people emerged ~2,000 years later.
